data.remark:
NeuralHorner: one modulus-conditioned recurrent cell (~471K-parameter GRU) run in a fixed bit-serial Horner loop, computing (a*b) mod p. The cell learns the per-step transition s' = (2s + d*x) mod p; the same weights reduce a, reduce b, and multiply the two residues. On the official open-source scorer it clears all ten tiers at exact-match 1.00 across three seeds, within the time budget (the competition's automated evaluation scored it 100% at 260s on submission; an automated score, not a human verification).

Key idea: the arithmetic is learned, the schedule is not. A single shared cell, conditioned on the modulus, transfers to primes it never saw in training, where a monolithic learner reports near-zero cross-prime transfer. Inference sizes the per-step state to each prime's bit-length, which is exact and keeps the ten-tier run under budget.

Learned, not a circuit: randomizing the weights collapses every tier to 0 (the weight-perturbation anti-cheat). The forward path has no symbolic math, no big-integer modular multiply, no lookup table, and no compare-against-p on the operands.

 a held-out adversarial battery scores 759/768; the only failures are power-of-two-adjacent (Fermat) operands. A Lean 4 proof covers the integer double-and-add algorithm the loop imitates.

Code and research: github.com/Robby955/neural-horner
